newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-London stocks storm higher with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-London stocks storm higher with Wall Street.

text.p: London shares were pulled to a record close on Tuesday by another surge in Wall Street's rampant bull market, while the dollar also enjoyed a strong rally against the German mark.
But French and German stocks were left nursing modest losses because of by worries over European economic and monetary union (EMU).
All three bourses opened weaker but rallied gently during the morning, then Wall Street opened higher again after two straight record closes, but only London chased it higher.
London's FTSE index of leading shares closed with a gain of 52.9 points, or 1.13 percent, at 4,739.6 points, demolishing resistance at 4,700 and sailing past the previous high of 4,723 set on May 16.
"Wall Street was a very big help today," said one London
dealer. "There were no sellers around and shares are being continually squeezed higher...it's a combination of the lack of selling and the huge amount of liquidity in the market."
Wall Street was up over 80 points at the close of European business having passed 7,500 points at around 7,560.
The Dow has surged more than 1,000 points since the start of 1997 and is now benefiting from the dollar's recent weakness which is boosting shares in big U.S. exporting companies.

But British investors were likely to become more cautious ahead of the government's first budget on July 2 and on fears that the uncertainty over EMU could soon bleed into UK financial markets, dealers said.
In stark contrast with London, France's CAC 40 index closed lower in relatively light volume as investors took their cue from uncertainty over the euro to book profits.

Traders said the market needed to consolidate after the surprise rise since the Socialist election win. The bourse shrugged off Wall Street's attack on the 7,500 level and London's record high. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 22.02 points or 0.82 percent at 2,664.18.
Paris was extending Monday's steep fall on concerns over France's wrangling about the stability pact designed to ensure budgetary discipline under EMU.
French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn and other European Union officials on Monday said a delay in approving the stability pact was not a precursor to renegotiating it.

The German share market also fell and the DAX index, which closes before Wall Street opens, ended down 2.42 points at 3,665.01. A more stable day on the currency markets helped calm the market, which dipped as low as 3,648.45 early in the session.

Worries about monetary union and the future of Bonn's ruling coalition, still in the grip of a damaging dispute about how to plug Germany's gaping deficit hole, unsettled the market from the start and kept turnover minimal.

Dollar volatility always unsettles the German share market, since so many top German companies -- notably carmakers, engineering and chemical firms -- depend on the U.S. export market for large amounts of their sales.

Meanwhile the dollar rose more than a pfennig against the German mark, reversing much of Monday's mark rally as tensions surrounding preparations for Europe's single currency eased a touch. It ended at around 1.7180 in late European trade.
German, French and other senior politicians helped take the heated single currency debate off the boil by repeating their intention to start the project on time in 1999.

Monday's demand from the new French government for more time to consider the stability pact has shifted the market focus to the European Union summit in Amsterdam next week. For now, the markets are betting a solution will be found.

"We're all really just waiting here. This has turned into a big puzzle and people want to see the outcome of the summit before making any long-term changes to strategies," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.
French President Jacques Chirac today reaffirmed the government's committment to a punctual EMU start and said he hoped for a deal on the stability pact in Amsterdam summit.

Luxembourg prime minister Jean-Claude Juncker said he hoped the EU will find a solution to the impasse by the end of June and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi said French premier Lional Jospin has expressed a clear will to proceed with EMU.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7180 marks and 112.55 yen compared with 1.7063 marks and 112.55 yen on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 52.9 points at 4,739.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 22.02 points at 2,664.18.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended down 2.42 points at 3,665.01. In post-bourse electronic trading the DAX Ibis ended up2.55 points at 3,671.16.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1545 GMT
Gold closed at $3443.75 compared with Monday's close of $344.25.
